title: Push Slider
summary: A wall stands in front of the hovering aerial manipulator, with a horizontal slider mounted on its front face: a straight rail about 1 m long and a red knob that slides along it. The knob starts at the rail's left end (as seen from the robot facing the wall) and must be pushed along the rail until it is within 5 cm of the right end of its travel, i.e. at least 0.95 m along its 1 m travel.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane. In front of the robot stands an immovable (kinematic) wall: a slab 0.1 m thick, 2.0 m wide and 2.0 m tall with a concrete-block surface, its front face turned toward the robot. The wall is upright (no tilt in this task); its distance and sideways offset vary between instances. On its front face a slider fixture is mounted horizontally: a fixed rail 1.02 m long and 6 cm tall (a shallow channel standing about 3 cm out from the wall) and a red knob (a 4 x 4 x 6 cm block on a short stem, protruding about 7 cm from the wall surface) that slides along the rail over 1 m of travel. The fixture's height and sideways position on the wall vary between instances. The knob has no spring (it stays where it is left) but its motion is resisted by joint friction and damping. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the wall, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Wall: kinematic cuboid 0.1 (x) x 2.0 (y) x 2.0 (z) m, nominal centre (2.0, 0.0, 1.0) m and orientation identity (front face the plane x = centre_x - 0.05, normal -x, toward the robot); friction 1.0 static / 1.0 dynamic, restitution 0; visual material NVIDIA Concrete_Block.mdl. At each reset (Isaac Lab mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) the centre becomes (2.0 + dx, 0.0 + dy, 1.0) with dx, dy ~ U(-0.2, 0.2) m independently; the configured pitch range is (-0, 0), so the wall keeps the identity orientation (upright, front normal -x). Slider: articulation slider_with_rail.usd with a fixed root body 'Rail' and self-collisions disabled. At each reset, after the wall, its root is placed at wall_centre + R_wall (-0.05, sy, sz) with sy, sz ~ U(-0.3, 0.3) m independently (on the wall's front face) and given the orientation R_wall composed with a 180 degree rotation about z, so the rail's local +x points toward the robot (world -x) and its local +y is world -y. Rail (rail frame, scaled 1.02 along y): base box 0.02 (x) x 1.02 (y) x 0.06 (z) m centred on the wall surface (half of it inside the wall), upper and lower edges 0.02 x 1.02 x 0.01 m at x = 0.02, z = +-0.025, edge covers 0.01 x 1.02 x 0.02 m at x = 0.025, z = +-0.018; mass 1 kg; no visual material bound. Knob (body 'Slider', gravity disabled, mass not authored so PhysX derives it from the collision shapes, colour (1, 0, 0)): a base plate 0.005 x 0.02 x 0.03 m at x = 0.017, a short connector cylinder, and a handle box 0.04 (x) x 0.04 (y) x 0.06 (z) m centred 0.052 m in front of the rail plane. Prismatic joint SliderJoint along the rail's local +y (world -y), limits [-0.5, 0.5] m, reset to -0.5 m with zero velocity every episode (knob at world y = root_y + 0.5, the robot's left end); positive motion moves the knob toward world -y. Isaac Lab implicit actuator (overriding the USD drive): stiffness 0, damping 5.0, joint friction 4.0 (static and dynamic), effort limit 1000, velocity limit 2.0 m/s. Scene default physics material: friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0.
success: Success when the slider's prismatic joint SliderJoint has position >= 0.45 m (slider_pushed_threshold; the joint ranges from -0.5 m to 0.5 m and starts at -0.5 m), i.e. the knob has travelled at least 0.95 m from its start toward world -y (the robot's right). AM-Bench also reports a subtask criterion slider_engaged (joint position - start >= 0.05 x (0.45 - (-0.5)) = 0.0475 m); it is informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 26 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 3120 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 3119th step.
difficulty_note: The knob has to be driven 0.95 m, almost the whole length of the rail, in one direction against joint friction and damping, and the fixture's place on the wall changes per instance.
standard_notes: The fixture's pose and the knob's position along the rail are not given: the red knob and the rail on the concrete wall have to be located with the onboard cameras, and progress is visible only as the knob's position along the rail. Left and right refer to the robot's view of the wall at reset.
